title: The Hot Soup and Cold Winter
summary: The village elders bet Nasruddin that he could not spend an entire freezing winter night on the snowy mountain peak without a fire, coat, or blanket. If he survived, they would buy...
keywords: the hot soup and cold winter
full_text:
The village elders bet Nasruddin that he could not spend an entire freezing winter night on the snowy mountain peak without a fire, coat, or blanket. If he survived, they would buy him a grand feast.

Nasruddin accepted the wager, stood on the freezing summit all night, and survived by watching a tiny candle flame flickering in a farmhouse window a mile away.

The next morning, the greedy elders refused to pay: "You warmed yourself by the candle light a mile away! You lost the bet!"

Nasruddin said nothing. He invited them to dinner that evening. The guests arrived hungry, but after two hours, no food appeared. Looking into the kitchen, they saw Nasruddin holding a giant cauldron of soup suspended from the ceiling, with a tiny candle burning on the floor five feet below it!

"Mulla, are you crazy?" shouted the elders. "How can a candle five feet below boil a giant pot?"

"If a tiny candle a mile away could keep me warm through a winter blizzard," replied Nasruddin, "it can surely boil your soup in a few days! Sit down and wait!"

The ashamed elders apologized and paid the bet in full.
moral: Technical hair-splitting used to deny a fair reward deserves an equally absurd response.
